other_material_facts.value: TO FINANCE THE CAPITAL EXPENDITURE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE PURCHASE OF EQUIPMENT/ MACHINERIES FOR EXISTING MANUFACTURING FACILITY Our Company is engaged in the business of manufacturing, distribution, marketing and selling of bakery products in savoury category which include breads, buns, pizza bases, Kulcha etc. under our brand ‘American Bakers’, primarily catering to the local consumers.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: This is to further submit that despite the availability of installed machinery and equipment, the absence of supportive machinery automation in certain stages of our manufacturing process restrict our ability to increase our production efficiencies and overall production capacity.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: In order to strengthen our manufacturing capabilities and support the future growth of our business, our Company proposes to utilise up to Rs. 442.205 lakhs towards the purchase and installation of additional bakery processing machinery and equipment at its existing manufacturing facility.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: The proposed machinery and equipment include dough mixers, dough divider, dough rounder, dough moulder with auto panning system, swing tray proofer, swing tray oven, swing tray cooling chamber, conveyors, depanner and other allied machinery and equipment, which will further automate the various key stages of our manufacturing process.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: Moreover, the proposed machinery and equipment is also expected to improve our product consistency and quality, optimise production cycle time, enhance handling and processing capabilities, strengthen food safety and quality control measures and support higher production throughput.

other_material_facts.label: acquisition_investment
other_material_facts.value: We believe that the proposed investment in our manufacturing infrastructure will enhance operational efficiencies, improve overall productivity and strengthen our competitive position in the bakery products industry.

other_material_facts.label: acquisition_investment
other_material_facts.value: Accordingly, the proposed acquisition of machinery and equipment forms an integral part of our growth strategy and is expected to support the long-term expansion, scalability and operational efficiency of our business.

strategy_growth.risk: Such geographical concentration of our business in this region heightens our exposure to adverse developments related to competition, as well as economic and demographic changes in this region, which may adversely affect our business prospects, financial conditions and results of operations.

Further, as we enter into new markets and geographical areas, we are likely to compete with other players, who might have an established presence, and are more familiar with business practices and have stronger relationships with local customers, relevant government authorities, suppliers or are in a stronger financial position than us, all of which may give them a competitive advantage over us.

concerns_observed: Sole manufacturing facility is leased, not owned; lease from Ms. Neha Yadav at Rs. 45,000/month runs January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028.

100% of the proposed capex machinery/equipment orders (Rs. 442.21 lakhs, quoted by ARR Food Processing Tech India Private Limited, quotation valid only 4 months from May 19, 2026) have not been placed; no second-hand equipment restriction noted but timeline risk is explicit.
Bread accounts for 99.90% of product revenue in 9M FY26 (up from 92.10% in FY23), making revenue highly dependent on a single product category.
Uttar Pradesh accounts for 99.32% of revenue in 9M FY26, versus a broader spread across UP/Haryana/Delhi/Karnataka/West Bengal as recently as FY24.

Capacity utilization fell from 93.36% (FY23) to 78.61% (FY24), 84.39% (FY25) and 64.74% (9M FY26, not annualised) even as installed capacity rose from 7,424 to 9,472 TPA, with further IPO-funded capex adding to already under-used capacity.

Working capital gap widened from Rs. 511.58 lakhs (FY23) to Rs. 851.33 lakhs (FY24), Rs. 1,078.06 lakhs (FY25) and Rs. 1,382.61 lakhs (9M FY26); trade receivables rose from 11.43% of revenue (FY23) to 23.35% (9M FY26) with debtor days rising from 42 to 85.
None of the Objects of the Issue (Rs. 442.21 lakh capex, Rs. 750.00 lakh working capital, Rs. 675.00 lakh debt repayment) have been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
Negative operating cash flow was reported in FY23 (Rs. -152.41 lakhs) and FY24 (Rs. -17.28 lakhs).

verdict.our_read: Q&T Foods is a Ghaziabad-based wholesale bakery manufacturer selling breads, buns, pizza bases and Kulcha under the 'American Bakers' brand through 50+ dealers, with PAT scaling from Rs. 4.74 lakhs (FY23) to Rs. 297.63 lakhs (9M FY26), but the entire Rs. 442.21 lakh capex, single leased facility (lease to December 31, 2028), 99.90% Bread and 99.32% Uttar Pradesh revenue concentration, and declining capacity utilization (93.36% FY23 to 64.74% 9M FY26) sit on Objects that are unappraised and have no monitoring agency.
post_listing_commitments: Equipment capex of Rs. 442.21 lakhs scheduled for deployment in FY 2026-27.
Working capital deployment of Rs. 400.00 lakhs in FY 2026-27 and Rs. 350.00 lakhs in FY 2027-28.

Repayment/pre-payment of Rs. 675.00 lakhs against the State Bank of India cash credit facility (sanctioned Rs. 1,100.00 lakhs; outstanding Rs. 1,096.42 lakhs as on May 31, 2026), scheduled in FY 2026-27.

Promoter lock-in: minimum 20% promoter contribution locked for 3 years from the date of Allotment; Promoters' excess shareholding locked 50% for 2 years and the remaining 50% for 1 year from the date of Allotment; other pre-Issue shareholders locked 1 year from the date of Allotment.
red_flags: Three KMP/board departures within roughly 13 months pre-IPO: CFO Ashish Gautam (resigned October 27, 2025), Company Secretary Sarvagya Goel (resigned January 15, 2025) and Independent Director Devesh Arora (resigned August 30, 2025); replacement CFO Debal Pratim Sur was appointed only January 1, 2026.
40 instances of delayed Registrar-of-Companies filings (CHG-1, ADT-1, MGT-7, AOC-4, DIR-12, DPT-3, MGT-14) spanning FY2019-20 to FY2025-26, with delays ranging from 6 to 2,435 days.

Statutory-dues delays: Provident Fund payments delayed up to 2,435 days (some regularised only in 2024-2026) and GST filings delayed across FY23-FY26, including GSTR-1 delayed 443 days and GSTR-3B delayed 355 days in FY26.
Outstanding litigation totaling Rs. 87.12 lakhs (Company: 11 matters/Rs. 51.11 lakhs; Promoters: 10 matters/Rs. 36.01 lakhs), equal to 29.27% of PAT and 8.70% of net worth.
Promoters' average cost of acquisition is near zero versus the Issue Price: Nishant Raj Gupta Nil; Usha Gupta, Khushbu Varshney and Rakesh Gupta Rs. 1.14 per share each.
No monitoring agency has been appointed for fund deployment because the issue size falls below the Rs. 5,000 lakh SEBI ICDR threshold; deployment is overseen only by the Audit Committee/Board.
Audit reports/financial statements for FY19-FY23 issued by the erstwhile statutory auditor did not carry the ICAI-mandated UDIN.
strengths_observed: PAT grew from Rs. 4.74 lakhs (FY23, 0.13% margin) to Rs. 273.55 lakhs (FY25) and Rs. 297.63 lakhs in 9M FY26 (7.11% margin); EBITDA margin rose from 2.25% (FY23) to 12.02% (9M FY26).
Top-10 customer concentration declined from 33.00% of revenue (FY23) to 31.56% (FY24), 24.85% (FY25) and 24.97% (9M FY26).
Operating cash flow turned positive: Rs. 189.11 lakhs (FY25) and Rs. 112.61 lakhs (9M FY26, not annualised), reversing Rs. -152.41 lakhs (FY23) and Rs. -17.28 lakhs (FY24).
None of the Promoters' Equity Shares are pledged or otherwise encumbered, per the shareholding-pattern disclosure.
Sole manufacturing facility is ISO 22000:2018 and HACCP certified, and won 'Best regional emerging bakery of the year' at the Indian Pride Awards 2020.
